newsitem.title: UK: UK to focus on int'l financial laws, flows at G7.
newsitem.headline: UK to focus on int'l financial laws, flows at G7.

text.p: Britain will focus on international financial regulation and progress towards removing barriers to free capital flows at this weekend's Group of Seven (G7) meeting in Berlin, British government officials said on Thursday.

Britain was interested in hearing what work has been done on an initiative at the Lyon G7 gathering last year to develop a "lead regulator" to handle international financial crises, a UK official said.
"If a crisis like BCCI or Barings arises again, we're interested in making sure that the G7 countries can meet quickly and open up channels of communication quickly," he said.
Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke is expected to bring up capital flows issues because Britain is keen to encourage more progress in removing barriers to free capital movements.
"The Chancellor will be raising a point that we've been trying to make -- that IMF (International Monetary Fund) articles should be up to date on capital flows," the official said.
"They haven't caught up with the fact that capital controls have been removed more and more across the world," he said, adding this area amounted to more than "good housekeeping."

Officials said other issues expected to arise at the meeting of finance ministers and central bankers from the U.S., Germany, Japan, Britain, France, Italy and Canada include where things stand on Russia, the highly indebted poor country initiative and IMF quotas and equity allocations.
